title: A fraud score inside a checkout
summary: Score each payment for fraud fast enough that an honest customer never notices.
context: Jalebi Pay processes payments for 30,000 small merchants. A model flags likely fraud, and it needs recent behaviour: how many payments this card made in the last hour, and how old this device is. A checkout leaves about 100 ms for the score.
Fraud patterns move within weeks. Blocking a good customer costs a sale and a merchant's trust, and letting fraud through costs the money itself.
must_handle: A score arrives inside 100 ms at the 99th percentile, or the payment proceeds under fallback rules.
Features computed for serving match the ones used in training.
A new model can be tried on a small share of traffic and rolled back in minutes.
Every decision can be explained to a merchant later.
The true outcome arrives weeks later, as a chargeback, and must reach training.
show_in_answer: The path of one payment through scoring.
Where recent-behaviour features are computed and kept.
What happens when the model service is slow or down.
How a new model goes live, and how you judge it when outcomes are weeks away.
